reason: R0 is a passive pull-up load; if another load/feedback exists at system level (or you only care that the transistor stack still switches/amplifies), removing it often keeps the core signal path (VIN1 → net012 → VOUT1 via M4) intact. Caveat: without some pull-up path, VOUT1 may float high-impedance or get stuck low depending on leakage and operating point.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (function can remain, but output DC bias/swing may degrade)

reason: M0 appears to generate/condition the bias node IB2 (and/or sink current from IB1) using VB1; if IB2 is provided externally as a bias (ideal source or separate bias network), M0 can be deleted without affecting the VIN1-to-output signal transistor chain. Caveat: if IB2 depends on M0, removing it will collapse the bias for M4 and the circuit may stop operating.
impact_estimate: Low (only if IB2 is supplied elsewhere); High otherwise

reason: M3 is a PMOS tied to VDD that biases/loads the net012/IB1 region; if IB1 is driven externally (or if you accept a different operating point), removing M3 typically doesn’t break the basic amplification path through M1 and M4. Caveat: net012’s DC point and gain can change significantly; you may lose the intended biasing and the stage can saturate.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (mostly impacts biasing and gain, not the existence of a signal path)
